findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean-squared-distance and the FLOWR endpoint VJP, so all coordinate contrasts below are reward-shaping diagnostics rather than measured affinity effects.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.00-0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5]; recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so no observed label carries absolute affinity information and no terminal affinity benefit can be computed from the supplied evidence.

The information audit is explicitly not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian; its compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS is small (whole-window mean about 0.081 A, batch-bootstrap CI roughly 0.070-0.092) and the chosen-teacher score correlation is weak (about 0.10 compressed, 0.064 full), so the geometric teacher signal is a modest, non-causal diagnostic rather than evidence of affinity gain.

The curve-support selection retained 24 features under a strict rule (absolute integrated z >= 0.1, batch direction fraction >= 0.857, q < 0.05, scale floor excluded) with a fidelity rule of relative RMSE <= 0.35 and zero strong sign conflicts; this is a selection-enrichment criterion, not an absolute geometric descriptor of the pose.

The continuous-trend rows read so far are all observed-node linear fits with polynomial_accepted=false and extrapolation_allowed=false, and they show large first-to-last rate reversals with multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass first_rate_z about +9.3 to last_rate_z about -10.0 with 4 sign changes; landmark_00_local_dy about -72.4 to +5.5 with 6 sign changes), so a constant rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule must stay inside the observed node support.

Lineage support covers 14 independent batches and 700 batch nodes, but 349 nodes have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 fewer than 6, with at most 2 teachers per batch; ancestral coverage is therefore thin for most nodes and survival/terminal-credit statistics are multiple-testing adjusted over 400 survival tests, not terminal affinity effects.

Terminal metadata place the terminal score time at 0.99 and terminal state time at 1.0, outside the observed score window [0.0,0.5], with one future-resampling node per batch; last-record or terminal credit is therefore unobserved in this window and cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

hypotheses.direction: Prefer a validated observed-node time-conditioned contrast over a constant rule for these features; keep the rule inside [0.0,0.5].
hypotheses.falsifier: A constant contrast matching or exceeding the time-conditioned fit's relative node RMSE with no strong sign conflicts would remove the advantage of time conditioning.
hypotheses.observable: Sign and magnitude of the observed-node contrast for landmark soft-mass and local displacement features across the score-time grid.
hypotheses.scope: Observed score window 0.0-0.5, predicted endpoint world-A features, 14 independent batches.
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast over the observed score nodes (rather than a constant contrast) is the better-supported form for the landmark soft-mass and local-displacement features, because their observed-node linear fits reverse sign within the window.

hypotheses.direction: Treat teacher-overlap and score-correlation contrasts as descriptive diagnostics, not as an affinity target.
hypotheses.falsifier: A decoded terminal affinity comparison showing a reproducible benefit tracking the teacher-alignment contrast would weaken this limitation.
hypotheses.observable: Compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS and chosen-teacher score correlation with batch-bootstrap CIs.
hypotheses.statement: The geometric teacher-alignment signal is weak and non-causal, so a coordinate intervention justified only by teacher-overlap or chosen-teacher score correlation should not be expected to improve final predicted affinity.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or outcome evaluation data are supplied, so final predicted affinity benefit cannot be measured and last-record/terminal credit is not evidence of affinity gain.
The information audit is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian; its excess-distance metric is nonnegative by construction and is not a causal affinity effect.
Only the first six continuous-trend rows were read; the remaining 194 rows and the 24 curve-fidelity entries were not inspected, so feature-level conclusions are partial.
Ancestral coverage is thin (349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors, 531 with fewer than 6), so survival and turnover statistics are weakly supported for most nodes.
No temperature edit is permitted and none is proposed; temperatures are immutable task parameters.
